I am an Assistant Data Science Specialist at the University of Arizona Libraries in the Data Cooperative, which supports data-intensive research at UA. I primarily provide Python programming support to researchers across campus, though I also have experience with R and SQL, among other languages. 

My background is in using programming for data analysis as well as machine learning, with a specific focus on natural language processing (NLP) and computational social science (CSS). 

I am also currently a PhD candidate in the College of Information Science, where I am working with sociologists and information science researchers to investigate topics at the intersection of science of science and NLP. I am a certified Carpentries instructor and a Posit Data Science Mentor, in addition to previously being a lead instructor for undergraduate programming and data science courses at UA.
